newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Broken Hill Proprietary Petroleum of Australia will undertake oil and gas exploration activities in Sindh and Balochistan provinces with minimum financial commitment of $600,000.
- The wheat prices have been increased to discourage its illegal movement and provide incentives to farmers to help attain self-sufficiency in food production, says Food Minister Abida Hussain.
- More than 40 under-trial prisoners, who were being escorted back to Sargodha Jail after appearing in Bhalwal court escaped after a clash with police guards in central Pakistan.
- The government has decided to strictly utilise all future privatisation proceeds for debt servicing to bring it down to a manageable level.
- The World Bank believes the rupee will be over-valued vis-a-vis the dollar by 13 to 14 percent in the coming days.
- Japan is willing to negotiate with Pakistan the issue of anti-dumping duty on Pakistani yarn.
- The U.S. exports to Pakistan in 1996 rose 36 percent but Washington is still unhappy complaining that Pakistan protection continues to restrict U.S. exports.
- The government is actively considering to expedite work on export processing zones.
- India has ruled out talks with Pakistan on the disputed Kashmir issue during a two-day ministers' conference of the Non-Aligned Movement.
